submission.natural_language_explanation: N567− fires on the sequence-initial residual state, not on any token class: at a text's first token it is high for essentially every token (the recorded first-token floor — median ~1600 over a 1,500-token vocabulary sample, 95% of it above 0.8·max), and it repeats that same peak at any later position whose preceding tokens are all that one token, because attention over identical copies leaves the layer-21 pre-MLP state identical to position 0's (cosine 1.0000, activation equal to the decimal; SwiGLU g+41/u−40 in both cases); the same unit's positive pole never exceeds 3.6 on the scan, so it is one-sided. Hence on measured positions (everything but the first token) it is active exactly when the opening token ids repeat — the text opens with the same token twice or with a longer run of one token ('22', '2222', ' the the', ' loan loan', 'abab', a doubled tab or danda, ' - -') — and silent for ordinary openings ('23', ' the cat') and for a duplicate that follows any different token ('the cat sat sat', 'a the the', '22 22 22' past the space); the match is at the token-id level, so 'loan loan' at a line start (no leading space) is not a repeat, and rare near-duplicate states (' OR IMPLIED', 'γμα') reach only 20–30% of peak, below the 0.8·max active line.
rival_explanations: It is an immediate-duplicate (stutter) detector that fires whenever the current token equals the token just before it, wherever that happens in the text, so a repeated word mid-sentence after other words should activate it too.
It is a start-of-text positional neuron that fires at the second token of any text regardless of content, and the duplicate openings dominate the top examples only because the scan ranked them first.

It is a no-surprise/fluency detector that fires when the current token is fully predictable from its context, so it should also fire on strong fixed bigrams such as ' OR IMPLIED' and on near-certain words inside ordinary fluent prose.
